attacks.label: Crop 4 px from left and top (image becomes smaller)

interpretation: High PSNR/SSIM means the stego image looks like the cover; it does not prove resistance to steganalysis.
Capacity depends on the patch: block methods need complete 8x8 / 2x2 blocks inside the mask, edge-adaptive LSB needs edges.
Exact extraction from an unmodified PNG does not establish robustness to lossy transforms.
HUGO/WOW/S-UNIWARD minimise a distortion model; that is not a proof that no steganalyst can detect the message.
label: Educational experiment - not a live UAV transmission

metric_definitions.ber: (wrong bits + missing bits) / expected payload bits; 1.0 if extraction failed entirely
metric_definitions.capacity_bits: capacity measured by the algorithm implementation on this patch mask (not a knowledge-base estimate)
metric_definitions.embed_ms: patch embedding duration (perf_counter); setup_ms = cost evaluation inside it (STC methods)
metric_definitions.mse: mean over all samples of the IMAGE of (cover - stego)^2
metric_definitions.outside_patch_changes: samples changed outside the patch mask (must be 0)
metric_definitions.patch_mse: mean over the samples of the chosen PATCH only of (cover - stego)^2
metric_definitions.patch_psnr_db: 10 log10(255^2 / patch_mse); null when the patch is unchanged
metric_definitions.psnr_db: 10 log10(255^2 / MSE) over the image; null when MSE = 0 (identical images)
metric_definitions.robustness: per attack: extraction from the attacked image with the known patch mask and parameters (oracle); outcome recovered (BER 0) / partial (BER <= 0.1) / failed (BER ~0.5 is chance level)
metric_definitions.ssim: mean SSIM over the image, uniform 7x7 window, K1=0.01, K2=0.03, L=255

patch.note: kb_retrieval_readonly shows what the production selector would rank for this patch and payload; the experiment runs every requested algorithm regardless and changes nothing in production.

payload_construction.key: TEST-ONLY key = HKDF-SHA256(public label) -- not secret, never used for UAV traffic, not displayed
payload_construction.note: The same AppWire bytes are embedded by every algorithm in this comparison. The live transport additionally wraps them in Frame v1 (12-byte header + 32-byte HMAC) bound to the algorithm id.
payload_construction.serialisation: UTF-8 message bytes -> ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (header bound as associated data) -> AppWire v1
